name: Conservation Partner Grants
summary: Annual small grants to nonprofit and governmental partners that protect grizzly bear habitat, including private land conservation, and prevent conflicts between bears and people, such as retiring conflict-prone grazing leases.

steps: Two-page proposal (budget, photos, maps) as a PDF by email

eligibility.rule: Is a US or Canadian non-profit, or a state, federal or tribal body focused on science-based wildlife management
Is a 501(c)(3) or names a 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsor
Prevents bear-human conflicts and benefits occupied, planned or connecting grizzly bear habitat

deadline.text: Applications will be accepted until March 15, 2026

status.quote: Applications will be accepted until March 15, 2026, with awards announced in early May.

deadline.quote: Applications will be accepted until March 15, 2026, with awards announced in early May.

applicant_types.quote: Vital Ground offers grants to nonprofit or governmental entities whose missions complement ours.

access.quote: Vital Ground offers grants to nonprofit or governmental entities whose missions complement ours.

window.quote: We typically call for grant proposals once per year and award 5-10 grants of $10,000 or less.

amount.quote: Proposals are generally funded for less than $10,000 and applications may not exceed $15,000.

co_finance_required.quote: Matching funding is required at a minimum ratio of 1:1.

effort.quote: Applications will be accepted until March 15, 2026
Send proposals via email as an attached pdf document to: bjohnson@vitalground.org

eligibility.quote: The proposal must be submitted by a qualified non-profit based in either the United States or Canada, or be a state, federal, or tribal entity focused on science-based wildlife management.
If the proposal is not submitted by a 501(c)(3) organization, the organization needs to obtain a 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsor for the funds to be passed through to.

The project or program proposed must prevent conflicts between bears and humans and benefit grizzly bear habitat that is currently occupied, documented in an approved federal, state or tribal wildlife management plan, or expected to promote connectivity between occupied or potential grizzly bear habitats.

co_finance.quote: Matching funding is required at a minimum ratio of 1:1.

after_award.quote: All grantees are required to provide a final report on October 1, 2025.
